title: Anodyne extensions are stable under pushout product with a monomorphism
statement: Let $i:A\to B$ and $j:C\to F$ be morphisms of small simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Products and pushouts are formed degree by degree in sets. A monomorphism means a map injective in each degree. Call a map anodyne if it has the left lifting property against every Kan fibration, where a Kan fibration means a map with the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$, $0\leq k\leq n$, with horns as in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-model-right-proper-core]. The left lifting property means that every commutative square with this map on the left and the given map on the right has a diagonal filler. If $i$ is a monomorphism and $j$ is anodyne, then the pushout-product map $$(B\times C)\amalg_{A\times C}(A\times F)\longrightarrow B\times F$$ induced by $1_B\times j$ and $i\times1_F$ is anodyne.
